labels.notes: Row partial and unmarked in both files. The label is cited as `defi:causal_Ealpha` — `ETT.tex:1335` inside the first 4000 characters of each docstring. The file's only bold near it is '**Not marked**'. No **`label`** appears in either file. Both quotes (l.1327–1333, l.1339–1340) match ETT.tex verbatim. Scope (1): sectorAtlas, isGXAtlas_sectorAtlas (one rotation per overlap, by exists_rotation), support_sectorAtlas (= regPart α), isPortly_regPart and isAEAtlas_sectorAtlas hold for every α > 0, under [Fact (0 < α)] only. singularGX α is ⟨maximalAEAtlas (Flat.isom 2) (sectorAtlas α), isAEAtlas_sectorAtlas.isMaximalAEAtlas_maximalAEAtlas⟩, the same construction as E0GX.singularGX (Causal/Port/E0GXStructure.lean:354). Scope (2), α ≠ 2π: source_inter_singLine_eq_empty, reg_eq (Reg = regPart), sing_eq (Sing = singLine), sing_nonempty. chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas_of_ne is proved through forall_chartIso_aeAtlas_of_reg_subset, as the block prescribes. Scope (3), α = 2π: twoPiChart is (refl ℝ) × coneTwoPiIsoEuclidean, equal by rfl to massiveTwoPiToMinkowski. It is a ChartIso and equals rotIsom c • chart k on the whole source of each sector chart. It lies in the maximal atlas by an explicit AELe from sectorAtlas to insert twoPiChart sectorAtlas. Hence Reg = univ and Sing = ∅. chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas_two_pi goes through chartIso_of_mem_maximalAEAtlas_of_agreeOn, the agreement off supp A coming from the transition from twoPiChart to r. hreg is in DEC-25's form: chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas reads '∀ r ∈ aeAtlas (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) (Massive α), ChartIso (massive α) (minkowski 2) r'. That is E0GX.chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas (E0GXStructure.lean:514) with the model swapped. hreg_family is exactly the hreg of existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 (Causal/GXSingularDEC25.lean:551) at Xα = fun κ => Massive κ.1, DY = massiveOf, DX = minkowski 2. The combined statements check out. reg_sing_cases is the dichotomy. exists_mem_aeAtlas_inter_singLine_iff is an iff, its ← direction witnessed by twoPiChart through (0, apex). chartIso_of_isAEChart_of_subset_reg gives (b′) at regular sources between any two models, from hreg by chartIso_model_of_subset_reg. chartIso_of_isAEChart_two_pi gives (b′) at every source from E_{2π}. The continuation lemma (Causal.EAlphaContinuation) checks out. exists_smul_devPt_of_ringBox takes an arbitrary F : Massive α → Minkowski 2, a time t₀, ε > 0, ρ > 0, and hF: on each ringBox t₀ ε ρ φ, φ ∈ ℝ, the sector chart is h • F. It assumes no continuity and no point of the line, so the core form needs no point of the line, as claimed. Its conclusion F(t, polar(ρ, φ)) = g • devPt t ρ φ, for every real φ ≥ 0, is what the docstring says. exp_mul_I_eq_one_of_ringBox takes φ = 0 and φ = κ: e^{iκ} = 1. coe_two_pi_eq_zero_of_ringBox takes φ = 0 and φ = 2π, adds InjOn on the circle, and gives 2π ∈ κℤ. eq_two_pi_of_ringBox combines them: κ = n·2π with n ≥ 1, and 2π = mκ with m ≥ 1, so κ = 2π. There is no case split on κ ∈ 2πℤ, and the closer's claim is correct. Every chart of the maximal atlas meets the hypotheses. compatible_of_mem_aeAtlas (EAlphaGX.lean:258) gives e.symm.trans (chart k) ∈ gxGroupoid for each k, which is the `he` of eq_two_pi_of_mem_source. exists_ringBox_of_mem_source then supplies hF on every circle of radius ρ < ε, from preconnectedness of the box (exists_smul_eq_on_of_isPreconnected), and InjOn comes from e.injOn on a ball inside e.source. eq_two_pi_of_mem_source_singLine turns x ∈ singLine into (x.1, apex). The label is partial, not narrower than claimed. The (G,X) sentence about every E≥0-manifold (l.1339–1341) is downstream. (b′) from E_κ, κ ≠ 2π, at sources meeting the line is disclosed as not done (T-ett-bprime-ealpha). The group is Flat.isom 2 = SO₀(1,2) ⋉ ℝ³ (Causal/Flat/Form.lean:198), disclosed under OQ-82.

build.notes: `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true` on scaffold/CausalScaffold/EAlphaContinuation.lean and on scaffold/CausalScaffold/EAlphaGX.lean: both exit 0 with no output. Both .oleans (13:43:45 and 13:43:49) are newer than their sources (13:41 and 13:42), so EAlphaGX was checked against the current EAlphaContinuation. After 13:30 only these two .oleans and the other target's SFA* .oleans were rebuilt, so nothing upstream moved. `sorry` appears in neither file's code: the two hits are the docstring heading 'What is proved (no `sorry`)'. There is no admit, native_decide, axiom, set_option, implemented_by or extern. No global instance is added: singularGX and singularGXFamily are local-instance abbrevs, and fact_pi_pos and fact_four_pi_pos are theorems made local instances. `#print axioms` was run on all 75 declarations the REPORT names (36 decls and 39 extra_decls), from a probe in /tmp/audit-eagx-probe that has been deleted. Each gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and every name resolved. Layering: the transitive local import closure of CausalScaffold.EAlphaGX, a superset of EAlphaContinuation's, has 64 modules. It contains no Causal.Port.E0*, no CBG, BTZ or Barbot module, and no Causal.Model.EAlphaCauchy. The only Causal.Port modules in it are SingularAtlas, GXBasic, Portly, Developing and UniversalCover, all mechanical model-free ports of gx (a.e. atlases, the (G,X) basics, portly sets, the developing theorem, universal covers). Causal.Port.SingularAtlas imports only Causal.Port.Portly (Mathlib) and Causal.Port.GXBasic (Causal.GXStructure and Mathlib). It is DEC-25's vocabulary, not the E₀ model, and EAlphaContinuation needs it for exists_smul_eq_on_of_isPreconnected (SingularAtlas.lean:371). EAlphaGX imports Causal.MaximalAEAtlasIso, not Causal.Port.E0GXStructure. Scope: `git status --short` shows this target's two untracked scaffold files and its campaign directory. The other entries are the three roadmap.toml status flips (atlas, programme and egf loops: status ready→active/done, not the closer) and the files of other live targets (SFATransfer, SFALocalE0, CurvesExtendSecondCountable, lean-egf). No tracked file under lean-causal/ changed, so Causal/Model/EAlphaCauchy.lean and Causal/Static.lean are untouched. The closer built its own two modules with `lake build`, which CAMPAIGN.md allows.

findings.what: Hypothesis checklist rows 'reg(E_α) an (Isom(E), E)-manifold' (✓ for α ≠ 2π, ⚠ at α = 2π: Reg ⊋ reg) and 'sing(E_α) the singular line' (⚠ Sing = ∅ at α = 2π) misuse the kb/0006 vocabulary. The paper's assertion that reg(E_α) carries an (Isom(E), E)-structure is proved at every α > 0, 2π included: isGXAtlas_sectorAtlas and support_sectorAtlas carry no α ≠ 2π hypothesis, and the REPORT's own finding 1 says 'as printed'. What changes at α = 2π is the identification of DEC-25's Reg/Sing with the paper's reg/sing. That is a reading, which belongs in SCOPE. It is neither a weakened nor a strengthened hypothesis. The same point was raised in T-ett-ealpha-sectors AUDIT-1.
findings.fix: At graduation, rewrite the reg cell as '✓ carried for every α > 0 (isAEAtlas_sectorAtlas, support_sectorAtlas), in DEC-25's atlas reading (SCOPE); Reg = reg(E_α) iff α ≠ 2π (reg_eq_regPart_iff)'. Rewrite the sing cell as 'a reading (SCOPE): Sing = sing(E_α) for α ≠ 2π (sing_eq); Sing(E_{2π}) = ∅ (sing_eq_empty_two_pi)'.

findings.what: The question 'is E_{2π} a model with a marked singular line?' is not genuinely open. The paper settles it: l.1328 writes E_{2π} = E, and l.2185 uses the convention 'α = 2π if p is regular'. DEC-25 fixes Sing as the complement of the support of the maximal a.e. atlas, which leaves nothing to mark. DEC-74 records the author's own 'E_{2π} is regular' for the same family (gx §4). Finding 1 is true (sing_eq_empty_two_pi, reg_eq_univ_two_pi, reg_eq_regPart_iff). It is a statement-level wording remark on the notation paragraph l.1331–1333 ('the singular line' of E_{2π} = E is not singular), and it is harmless to every argument.
findings.fix: No OQ row. Record finding 1 in the defi:causal_Ealpha ledger notes as a wording remark at l.1332 ('for α ≠ 2π', or 'the line of E_{2π} is regular'), citing l.1328, l.2185 and DEC-74.

findings.what: Neither question needs a new OQ row. Question 2 (which (Isom(E), E)-structure on reg(E_α)) repeats T-ett-ealpha-sectors' question, which was graduated at 03d7f18 with no OQ row. As that audit noted, the metric of l.1329 singles the structure out, since the polar developments pull back -dt²+dx² to -dt²+dr²+r²dθ². Its only remaining freedom is the group. Question 3 is OQ-82, open and already recorded. On the group: every Lean statement in both files is stated for G = Flat.isom 2 = SO₀(1,2) ⋉ ℝ³ (Form.lean:198), and none for O↑(1,2) ⋉ ℝ³. The proofs use only rotIsom ∈ Flat.isom 2, Flat.isom_strongMorphism, IsRigidAction and faithfulness (eq_of_smul_eq_smul). Each of these holds for O↑ as well, and OQ-82's own text says spatial reflections preserve the causality. So no proof uses a property of SO₀ beyond its being the group parameter. Under an O↑ ruling the statements would have to be restated over the larger group, with a larger maximal atlas. The arguments carry over (prose, as the SCOPE says), but nothing of this is in Lean.
findings.fix: No OQ-86 from this target. Optionally add this target's anchors (EAlphaGX.singularGX, hreg_family) to what OQ-82 blocks.

findings.what: Finding 2 is true, but it is a confirmation of ETT.tex:1327–1328, not something the author needs to change. 'The paper never says so' should not reach the author as a correction. Two details. (a) The n ≥ 2 clause ('the linear holonomy is trivial and only the branching detects the singularity') is by hand. rotIsom (2πn) = 1 follows from rotIsom_eq_of_exp_eq, and the map (t, polar(r, θ)) ↦ (t, r e^{iθ}) of E_{4π} satisfies hF. That is true, but no Lean witness shows hF satisfiable at κ = 4π. (b) 'a chart compatible with the sector charts reaches the line iff α = 2π (exists_mem_aeAtlas_inter_singLine_iff)' misattributes the result: that iff is about charts of the maximal atlas. For merely compatible charts the → direction is EAlphaContinuation.eq_two_pi_of_mem_source.
findings.fix: Record it as a confirmation note in the ledger (l.1327–1328 confirmed under DEC-25 for α ≠ 2π: source_inter_singLine_eq_empty, eq_two_pi_of_ringBox), with the citation corrected and the n ≥ 2 holonomy remark labelled 'by hand'.

findings.what: Causal.EAlphaGX.isOpen_regPart duplicates the strict Causal.isOpen_regPart (Causal/Model/EAlphaCauchy.lean:556): same statement, and EAlphaCauchy's version is proved without the Fact. It is harmless here, because EAlphaCauchy is not in the import closure, which is deliberate while T-loc-ealpha-tidy holds that file. However, a later module that imports both and writes `open EAlphaGX` inside `namespace Causal` will get an ambiguous identifier. This is the same pattern as the sectorChart shadowing found in T-ett-ealpha-sectors AUDIT-1.
findings.fix: At graduation, rename it (e.g. isOpen_regPart_of_closed) or make it private. Alternatively, once T-loc-ealpha-tidy has moved Causal.isOpen_regPart to a module EAlphaGX may import, drop it and use the strict lemma.

findings.what: The scaffold root imports neither file, so the axiom sweep cannot see them (kb/0025), as the REPORT notes. EAlphaGX imports CausalScaffold.EAlphaContinuation, so the two must graduate together.
findings.fix: Add both modules to the root, EAlphaContinuation first. If they graduate into Causal/, also rewrite EAlphaGX's `import CausalScaffold.EAlphaContinuation` to the new module name.

findings.what: Both findings are true and both concern the roadmap, as the REPORT says. Finding 4: [r] (b) is wrong, since exists_smul_devPt_of_ringBox chains only the EAlphaSector disc charts and exists_rotation, at steps δ = sin(w)/2 on a circle of radius ρ. Finding 5: no case split on κ ∈ 2πℤ is needed (eq_two_pi_of_ringBox), so the fallback has no remainder. Neither should enter the paper's ledger as a paper finding. One caution for the planner, a note only: the box form's hF asks for a single F : Massive α → Minkowski 2 on all the boxes. For an a.e. chart E_κ ⇀ E_κ' through the line (T-ett-bprime-ealpha), such an F must first be assembled from sector charts of E_κ', which the lemma does not do.
findings.fix: Send findings 4–5 and the caution to the planner (roadmap evidence of T-ett-bprime-ealpha / JOURNAL). Mark T-ett-ealpha-gx-structure done with no split.
